prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury attorney in Chicago for a car accident claim?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” personal injury lawyer for every car-accident case in Chicago — the right attorney depends on the specifics of your case (severity of injuries, liability issues, insurance limits, whether there’s a possible lawsuit, etc.) and what you value (big-firm resources vs. personal attention, trial experience, language needs, etc.). I can help you find a strong match. Meanwhile, here’s how to narrow the field and choose a top lawyer for your case.

What to look for
- Focus and experience: attorney who regularly handles car-accident and bodily-injury claims (not a generalist).  
- Trial and verdict experience: many cases settle, but you want someone who will and can take the case to trial if necessary.  
- Track record: past settlements/verdicts and client testimonials for similar injuries.  
- Resources: in-house investigators, medical experts, and the ability to advance case expenses.  
- Communication and accessibility: clear points of contact and timely updates.  
- Peer recognition: listings on Super Lawyers, Martindale‑Hubbell AV Preeminent, Best Lawyers, or local awards can be signals (not guarantees).  
- No disciplinary history: check Illinois attorney registration and disciplinary records.

Where to search
- SuperLawyers, Avvo, Martindale‑Hubbell, Best Lawyers  
- Chicago Bar Association Lawyer Referral Service or Illinois State Bar Association referrals  
- Local hospital/medical provider recommendations (for serious injuries)  
- Google/Yelp reviews (read several; watch for patterns)

Questions to ask at a free consultation
- Have you handled cases like mine? What were the outcomes?  
- Do you try cases or mostly settle? How many jury trials in the last 5 years?  
- Who will handle my case day-to-day? Will I deal with the attorney or paralegals?  
- What is your fee structure and typical percentage? (contingency fees are common, usually ~33%–40% depending on stage/appeal)  
- Do you advance case costs? How are medical liens handled?  
- What is a realistic range of recovery for my injuries?  
- How long will resolution likely take?

Red flags
- Guarantees of a specific dollar amount.  
- Pressure to sign quickly.  
- Poor responsiveness or lack of written fee agreement.  
- No relevant experience or unwillingness to take the case to trial if needed.

If you want, I can:
- Look up and compare 3–5 highly rated Chicago personal-injury attorneys or firms near your zip code, or  
- Help you prepare for consultations by drafting case-specific questions, or  
- Review attorney profiles/advertisements you’ve found.

If you share your zip code and a few details about the accident and injuries (date of accident, severity, who was at fault, insurance limits if known), I’ll pull together tailored recommendations.
